ov: Flying insects that feed on nectar and pollen, with over 20,000 species. Honey bees and bumblebees live in colonies, but more than 90% of bee species live alone.

why.dm: The western honey bee was one of the first domesticated insects and is kept by beekeepers for honey and pollination.
why.dg: Honey bees sting to defend the hive, and the more aggressive Africanised bees have caused many deaths.
why.p: Honey bees are kept by beekeepers for honey and pollination rather than as pets.

rg: Every continent except Antarctica, wherever there are insect-pollinated flowering plants.
df: Nectar for energy and pollen for protein, which is mostly fed to the larvae.

cf.tip: Bees have branched, feathery hairs for carrying pollen and feed on nectar and pollen. Their close relatives the wasps are carnivores or omnivores.

fx: Honey bee workers born in spring and summer live only a few weeks.
